# Dynamic Swing Anchored VWAP (Zeiierman)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Dynamic Swing Anchored VWAP resets its reference at newly confirmed swings and weights recent observations more strongly through decay. It is intended to remain closer to current structure than a long cumulative anchored VWAP, making pullbacks and retests easier to inspect. The volatility-aware speed adjustment is a responsiveness choice rather than evidence that this reference is more trustworthy or a uniquely correct fair value.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** Swing confirmation, price/volume decay and ATR-adaptation equations are absent.

- Swing confirmation, price/volume decay and ATR-adaptation equations are absent.

## How it works

- Confirm swing highs/lows with the Swing Period and begin a new anchored average when market direction flips.
- Compute decayed price-times-volume averaging from the anchor; optionally modify tracking speed using ATR relative to average ATR.

## Outputs and intended use

- Use the line as a swing-relative value guide for trend pullbacks or discretionary mean-reversion analysis.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Swing Period, Adaptive Price Tracking in bars, ATR-ratio adaptation and Volatility Bias are configurable. Bias above 1 strengthens adaptation and below 1 weakens it; no defaults are given.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: pivot confirmation delays anchoring and adaptive decay differs from conventional cumulative VWAP; apparent pivot-origin lines may conceal availability timing.

# Session Edge Profiler | Flux Charts

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Session Edge Profiler measures completed-session behavior and compares the developing session with its own weekday-filtered history. It aims to replace generic claims about Asia, London or New York with instrument-specific evidence. The dashboard covers range, volume, directional persistence, daily extremes and explicitly defined structural counts. Its alert identifies unusually large range rather than a directional trade. The source provides enough parameterized lifecycle and metric rules to reproduce a substantive session-statistics specification, while realistic execution and future profitability remain outside its purpose.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** The source defines the financial computation and parameterized inputs sufficiently for a reproducible specification.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Track each enabled session’s OHLCV/events in New York time, commit completed records at the shifted trading-day boundary and filter history by selected weekday.
- Normalize session range by previous completed daily ATR; average normalized ranges and count historical values at/below the current normalized range for percentile.
- Bull means session close > session open. Continuation means its bullish/bearish direction matches the previous occurrence of that same session; exclude the first occurrence from the eligible denominator. Bull%=100×bull count/all sessions; Continuation%=100×matched count/eligible sessions. Volume share is session volume divided by summed completed enabled-session volume; daily-extreme flags compare session extremes with full trading-day extremes.
- At active-session bar t, bullish FVG is Low_t>High_(t−2), storing High_(t−2); bearish FVG is High_t<Low_(t−2), storing Low_(t−2). Later within the same session, invalidate/remove a bullish gap if close falls below its stored level or a bearish gap if close rises above its stored level. Survival%=100×(formed−invalidated)/formed at session end; later-session invalidation does not change that result.
- Confirm pivots with the chosen number of bars on each side. A subsequent close above a confirmed high or below a confirmed low increments the active-session swing-break counter and consumes that pivot so it cannot be counted again. A newly confirmed high above the previous tracked session high pivot increments HH; a newly confirmed low below the previous tracked session low pivot increments LL.

## Outputs and intended use

- Thirteen dashboard metrics, session boxes, live range/average/percentile label and high-percentile alert support session research.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Five default NY windows: Asia 19–02, London 02–08:30, NY AM 08:30–12, Lunch 12–13:30, PM 13:30–16. Day boundary 18:00 NY via six-hour shift.
- ATR length default 14, range 5–50; pivot strength default five each side, range 2–20. Weekdays default on, weekends off.
- Range alert exceeds 90th percentile. Tier cutoffs are 75/25 for percentile and 70/40 for FVG survival.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Live partial-session range is compared with complete historical sessions, so percentile is not time-of-session adjusted.
- Volume denominator is summed enabled completed sessions, not necessarily all market-day volume; overlaps can double-count.
- FVG survival means survival only until that session ends.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Tie/zero-denominator and interrupted-session edge cases need implementation choices; no trade-execution model is intended.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: intraday ohlcv, daily ATR history, New York timezone/session calendar.

Repository input-class support: unavailable or unresolved. The specification is substantive, but usable aligned intraday history/session coverage has not been established.

# Weekly Volume Heatmap

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Map typical weekly trading-volume patterns to identify relatively active and quiet hourly slots.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for slot-average volume divided by average weekly volume on caller-supplied hourly history and weekly/session partitions; calendar and incomplete-week policies must be chosen explicitly.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Group supplied one-hour volume history by weekday/hour slot and calculate each slot’s arithmetic mean from the first through last available bar. Divide that mean by average traded volume per week and multiply by 100 for the corresponding heatmap percentage.

- The tool works only on the one-hour timeframe. No timezone, sample-length default or missing-session adjustment is stated.

## Idea and objective

Realtime 5D Profile accumulates live chart updates into price-level distributions of volume or update counts. It encodes level activity, directional imbalance and age, offering an evolving view of where observed participation occurred. Unlike a historical profile, it starts when loaded and loses its accumulated state when refreshed or re-executed. The source carefully distinguishes chart updates from exchange transactions, so its tick label must not be interpreted as a complete trade tape on aggregated charts.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for up/down update-count totals/delta on supplied ordered updates with explicit first-update convention and timeframe reset. Volume extraction, level rebinning, age rendering and trend-reset parity remain incomplete.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Independent aggregate activity counts: for ordered chart updates, compare price with the previous update; increment UpCount on higher price, DownCount on lower price, and carry the last known direction when unchanged. Totals are UpCount+DownCount and delta UpCount−DownCount. Use a selected timeframe reset; seed from the first observed price and begin counting once a comparison/known polarity exists. This explicit first-update exclusion is a caller convention because source initialization is not stated.
- Assign each update to up/down using price versus the preceding update, retaining the last direction when unchanged.
- Bin updates around dynamic price levels; rebalance historical updates when the profile range changes. Line lengths scale to the largest level and age comes from average update times.
- Render double-sided down/up profiles or single-sided totals/deltas; reset by selected timeframes or trend changes.

## Outputs and intended use

- Compare participation and recency with line width, thickness, totals, tooltips and Data Window values.
- No alerts are included; the author suggests small-timeframe use with infrequent chart changes.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Four line thicknesses encode age. An example 20-level double profile needs 42 labels against a 500-label limit.
- The author reports handling upwards of 60K updates per profile, not a guaranteed capacity.
- Choose tick/update-count mode and a timeframe reset (chart timeframe resets each new bar). Caller first-update policy is explicitly excluded until direction is known; this is not claimed as default-code parity.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Live-only state cannot be reconstructed from historical OHLCV.
- Uptick/downtick classification can misclassify true aggressor flow; prolonged accumulation may exhaust memory.

# Trend Target Ribbon [BOSWaves]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Trend Target Ribbon combines ALMA trend confirmation with a chart-based position plan. A directional flip creates an entry reference, structural risk distance and staged reward levels, while a gradient ribbon conveys the strength of the existing trend.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for configured trend-state flips and ATR-clamped structural risk with caller calculation settings/initial state; ribbon conviction, target spacing and intrabar event ordering remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Configured trend rule: B=ALMA(source,length,offset,sigma), slope=(B-B[k])/ATR and band width=confirmation*SD(source,deviation length). Flip bullish only if slope>minimum and close>B+width, bearish only if slope<-minimum and close<B-width, and only on a changed state. At a flip entry E=close; long raw risk=E-lowestLow(stop lookback), short raw risk=highestHigh(stop lookback)-E. Clamp risk to [minimumATR*ATR,maximumATR*ATR] and place stop E-risk for long or E+risk for short. Caller supplies all selected calculation settings and initial state.
- The baseline is an ALMA of the selected source. Its change over a configurable slope lookback is divided by ATR. Bullish confirmation requires positive slope above its threshold and a close above the ALMA plus a standard-deviation confirmation band; bearish confirmation reverses both conditions. State changes only when the qualifying direction differs from the current state.
- On a flip, entry is the closing price. The recent swing low for longs or high for shorts supplies raw risk, clamped between minimum and maximum ATR distances. Successive equidistant R targets extend in the trade direction. Bar extremes track stops and target hits; an opposing flip freezes the previous drawing.
- Conviction blends doubled slope magnitude and price separation from ALMA to control a layered ribbon and candle brightness. Old position drawings are removed when the history limit is exceeded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Directional diamonds and alerts identify flips. Entry, stop, risk zone, target lines and persistent checkmarks support visual planning and staged discretionary exits. Proximity glow highlights approaching targets; faded plans preserve recent signal history.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Suggested baseline: ALMA length 34, confirmation 0.65, slope minimum 0.08, structural lookback 12, stop ATR bounds 0.75 and 3.0, four targets and four visible positions. Source, ALMA offset/sigma, slope/deviation lookbacks, projection length and approach radius are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Choppy markets can produce rapid opposing plans. ATR clamping can move a stop away from actual structure. Drawn target touches do not establish executable fills, intrabar event order or measured returns.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- ATR and deviation lengths, ALMA offset/sigma defaults, exact conviction normalization and R-spacing coefficient are not supplied. Simultaneous stop/target handling is not defined.

# real_time_candles

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** financial-library. Native publication type: library. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

real_time_candles builds candle objects from live samples of prices or other financial series. It supports chart-synchronized candles and independently sampled time/count candles, exposing both their OHLC state and drawing helpers. Its financial uses include watching an oscillator change within a bar or examining short-lived price structures. This is not merely a graphics utility: its central output is sampled financial-series candles, although the claimed trading edge is not validated by the description.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for synchronized ordinary sampled-source OHLC under the documented current/history state and carried-close reset. Custom-time units/overshoot, Heikin-Ashi and EMA implementations remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow chart-synchronized ordinary sampled-source OHLC: select candlestick style and wait_for_sync; begin at a new chart bar. Within a bar retain current source as Close, maximum/minimum of included source samples as High/Low and starting sample as Open. At subsequent chart boundaries the shown reset carries prior sampled Close into Open, seeds the new sample buffer with that Open and appends new observations; thus the carry is included in High/Low. Current object is index0 and completed objects are inserted at index1.
- Capture source values, elapsed milliseconds and sequential update indices with persistent intrabar state.
- Update the current candle at array index zero and preserve completed candles at later indices. Custom candles close when accumulated update count or elapsed time reaches the configured threshold.
- Expose candle arrays, single objects or tuples, standard/Heikin-Ashi styles, extracted components and EMA/drawing methods.

## Outputs and intended use

- Use candles as inputs for custom indicators or render them with time/bar-index coordinates and optional moving averages.
- The example labelled fast RSI actually extracts candle closes; it does not itself calculate a custom-timeframe RSI.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Examples include RSI length 14, 20-second candles with EMA 9 and 15-update candles. Recommended history is 5000 bars and drawing limits 500 each.
- Timezone display offsets span -12 to +12; tied_open connects a new open to the preceding close.
- Choose source (default close), ordinary CandleType.candlestick and synchronization to a new bar. For exact parity preserve the shown carried-close reset; starting/reconnection behavior outside synchronized complete bars is not specified.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Historical bars cannot recover missing live updates, so custom candles cannot be historically backtested from this source.
- An execution update is not necessarily a single exchange trade.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Full boundary overshoot/gap behavior, Heikin-Ashi recurrence and sampling-time units need clarification; the shown time threshold compares seconds against a duration documented in milliseconds.

## Idea and objective

Show localized directional pressure between price and an adaptive reference line, then mark fresh agreement of profile, price position and anchor slope.

- Colored-band cutoff

## How it works

- Divide the anchor-to-nearest-body-edge corridor into twelve bands. Aggregate sixty recent candles with recency emphasis; calculate normalized buy-minus-sell imbalance in each band using price, estimated volume delta or hybrid pressure.

## Outputs and intended use

- Green/red/transparent bands show buying/selling/weak pressure. Long labels require dominant green pressure, enough active bands, price above a rising anchor and fresh alignment; short labels reverse those conditions. The source explicitly denies true bid/ask delta.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Anchor choices are EMA/SMA/VWMA/VWAP/Donchian midpoint, length default twenty-one. Dominance defaults 0.25, active bands seven and same-direction signal spacing six bars. Localization, wick influence and intrabar resolution are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Pressure weights and selected color thresholds can change the signal materially. Candle-derived volume is a proxy and should not be represented as observed buyer/seller flow.

# OptiPine: High-Performance Caching and Data Pipelines

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** financial-library. Native publication type: library. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

OptiPine provides caching, sparse-update and reusable-storage infrastructure, with complete financial examples that make it relevant beyond a generic platform utility. A regime-stress example computes a probability-weighted downside scenario estimate, while a pivot-zone example clusters recent price levels and reports their strength. The library’s purpose is to avoid unnecessary computation and data movement without changing the financial model. Its advertised speedups are author benchmarks, not measurements performed here. The examples define reproducible calculations, but their outputs remain illustrative models rather than validated risk probabilities or support/resistance forecasts.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Source includes substantive parameterized computations/code that can be reproduced.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Memo/Watch track dependencies; cadence gates intentionally delay work; row rings retain bounded histories without shifts.
- StablePool maps persistent IDs to reusable slots; DirtySet processes changed objects; typed indexes/buckets accelerate key/group lookup.
- Stress example combines EMA spread in ATR units with ATR percentage and Gaussian-weighted shock scenarios. Zone example stores confirmed pivots, buckets prices by tick size and aggregates pivot-volume strength.

## Outputs and intended use

- Reusable APIs plus stress plot, pivot levels, strongest-cluster price and Data Window statistics support financial modeling infrastructure.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Stress example uses EMA20/50, ATR14 and scenarios -200..200 with shock divided by 40; trend is clipped ±3 and quantized to tenths, volatility to quarters.
- Zone defaults: pivot length 5, max zones 32, bucket size 25 ticks; user ranges bound capacity/strength.

# Volatility Risk Premium

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Volatility Risk Premium compares VIX-implied volatility with trailing realized volatility to describe the market’s apparent insurance premium. It aims to contextualize equity risk and option strategy selection, with regime labels, historical standardization and momentum. This is a backward-looking realized-versus-forward-looking implied comparison, not an ex-post matched-horizon variance premium. The source discusses academic evidence but does not validate this implementation or make its illustrative options applications risk-free. It is calibrated for S&P 500 context and explicitly warns that other assets require recalibration.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for chosen-lookback daily log-return realized volatility annualized by √252, VIX-minus-RV and default EMA5 smoothing. Missing N default, variance convention, other estimators and regime/reversal rules remain caveats.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow close-to-close output: compute daily log returns ln(C_t/C_(t−1)), their rolling standard deviation over chosen N daily returns, and annualize by √252. Express realized volatility on the same percent-volatility scale as VIX; raw VRP=VIX−annualized realized volatility, and displayed smoothed VRP is EMA(raw VRP,5) at the source default. Sample/population deviation convention and zero/missing observations remain parity caveats.
- Estimate realized volatility from close-return standard deviation, Parkinson high/low range or Garman-Klass OHLC, annualize and subtract from VIX.
- EMA-smooth the difference, classify regimes and compare short/long realized-volatility windows.
- Compute trailing z-score, percentile and momentum; flag extreme z-scores beginning to reverse.

## Outputs and intended use

- VRP/regime, duration, IV/RV, percentile/z-score, slope, momentum and mean-reversion state plus alerts support volatility-context research.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Close-return annualization uses √252; smoothing defaults five days; short/long windows ten/sixty days.
- Regimes described above 10, 5–10, 0–5, -2–0 and negative; last definition overlaps LOW.
- Z-score extremes ±2 relative to trailing year; momentum lookback is unspecified.
- For the usable close-return path, caller chooses realized-volatility lookback N; no main N default is stated. Five daily periods is the disclosed EMA smoothing default. Other RV estimators and regime labels are outside this narrow scope.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Regime prose overlaps for negative readings; exact boundaries are unclear.
- VIX volatility versus trailing RV is not the same as risk-neutral-minus-expected-realized variance.
- Selling volatility bears crash/tail risk and implementation costs.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Main RV lookback, full Garman-Klass equation, variance convention, z-score window, slope formula and exact reversal predicates are absent.

- Calculate the highest high and lowest low over that group and show the current close, symbol and timeframe in a status panel.

- The displayed window contains the latest 10 candles. The status panel can be disabled.
- Choose equal chart/request timeframe and caller symbol; require ten supplied bars. The latest candle may develop live, so current extrema/close can change.

- Current higher-timeframe candle values change while the candle is open.

# FiniteStateMachine

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** financial-library. Native publication type: library. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Make trading logic explicit as prioritized state transitions and concurrent-condition rules. Although the library also demonstrates traffic lights, its source explicitly combines technical conditions, position management and re-entry in a trading-strategy example, making it relevant execution infrastructure.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Matrix and concurrent-map matching, wildcard precedence, ordering, return contracts and text rule formats define reproducible state transitions.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- A matrix row maps current state plus one event to next state. Concurrent rules map state to ordered condition/output pairs; their winning event can feed the sequential matrix engine.
- Blank strings and ANY serve as wildcards. Specific state/event matches outrank event wildcards, then state wildcards, then full wildcards; first encountered rules break ties within priority.
- Text loaders trim and append rules. Adding to an existing map state combines its rules instead of overwriting them. Validators check declared states, duplicate/conflicting transitions, malformed fields and unreachable/no-entry-or-exit states.

## Outputs and intended use

- Returns a next-state or event string, or na when no match exists. Rule/validation tables help inspect and debug control flow.
- The demo routes EMA/gap/fractal/RSI conditions through idle, setup, entry, position, exit and re-entry states; their actual financial thresholds are not part of this specification.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Caller state array, current state, event or active-condition names, ordered matrix/map rules, strict-input/transition flags and table options.
- Matrix text uses current state | event | next state; concurrent text maps state | condition > output pairs.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Order-dependent rules can hide unintended priorities. Validation of rule structure cannot guarantee safe trading logic or correct venue state.
- The narrative says first row wins while detailed contracts establish specificity tiers; implementations must apply first-match ordering within those tiers.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Strict-mode edge semantics and the full trading demo’s indicator/order rules are not explained; these are outside the basic transition computation.

## Idea and objective

Machine Learning RSI classifies the current momentum environment by matching a multidimensional RSI fingerprint to historical labeled analogs. It aims to replace a simple threshold interpretation with adaptive feature importance, distance-weighted votes and quality gates. The learned conviction also changes Supertrend width. The source clarifies this is an online analog classifier, not a neural network. - Build RSI level, slope, acceleration, neutral distance, percentile, volatility, fast/slow spread and regime features.

- Confidence is an internal score, not established probability.

## Idea and objective

Market Structure Dashboard integrates trend, confirmed pivots, price zones, participation and session context across multiple timeframes. It exposes individual components and a weighted directional summary to distinguish agreement from conflict. Many components have substantive rules, but the combined publication remains incomplete because fair-value-gap indexing contradicts its introductory definition and higher-timeframe confirmation is unstated. Institutional-order language interprets price patterns rather than observing account activity.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for current-timeframe EMA trend and relative-volume tiers, with confirmed symmetric pivot procedure also explicit. FVG contradictions, HTF confirmation, session DST and composite parity remain caveats.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow current-timeframe EMA/volume outputs: E=EMA(close,9); bullish if Close>E, bearish if Close<E, with equality not specified. V%=100×Volume/SMA(Volume,20). Apply tiers in descending order: >200 EXTREME; else >120 HIGH; else >80 NORMAL; else >50 LOW; else VERY LOW. Thus exact threshold equality falls into the next lower tier; zero mean volume remains undefined. Independently, a pivot high/low must be strictly higher/lower than five bars on each side and becomes known only after the right five bars.
- Compare close with EMA and confirm symmetric pivots; classify successive highs/lows and combine latest types into structural bias.
- After a swing break, use the intervening lowest-low or highest-high candle as an order block, invalidated by a close through. Track swing breaches and close reclaims.
- Sum enabled bullish/bearish/neutral factors by timeframe weight, then divide by the maximum possible magnitude. Add volume/SMA and ATR/average-ATR states.

## Outputs and intended use

- Read timeframe rows, nearest zones, prior-period extremes and optional overlays.
- Use session context and weighted bias to support analysis rather than automatic execution.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Up to seven timeframes; EMA defaults 9, swing length 5 and ATR 14 with averaging lookback 20.
- Volume thresholds are 200%,120%,80%,50%; volatility boundaries 130%,70%; bias boundaries ±20%,±50%.
- Use current chart timeframe, EMA9 and volume SMA20; pivot strength defaults five per side. Narrow scope excludes FVGs, HTF requests and session clocks.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Pivot confirmation is delayed.
- FVG wording alternates first/third candles with current versus three bars ago, and touch versus full-gap mitigation.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Resolve FVG indexing/mitigation, higher-timeframe sampling and EST versus New York daylight-saving interpretation.

## Idea and objective

This chi-square research tool tests whether grouped prior market conditions and subsequent close direction are associated. ## Idea and objective

Higher-timeframe requests provides financial market-data timing infrastructure for indicators, stable alerts and strategy commands. It compares developing higher-timeframe prices with confirmed prior-bar prices and demonstrates why historical and live request timing can differ. Its substantive output is a confirmed higher-timeframe source series, with a deliberate confirmation delay. The publication is educational and uses a study declaration, but its implemented price retrieval directly supports financial calculations. The source describes the offset/lookahead technique rather than proving a universal non-repainting guarantee for arbitrary downstream code.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

**Disclosed principal calculation.** The explicit requested-context close[1] plus lookahead_on call, strictly-higher-timeframe guard and next-HTF-open timing define confirmed HTF price retrieval. Wrapper parity and downstream behavior remain caveats.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Require the requested timeframe to exceed the chart timeframe; reject equal or lower timeframes with a runtime error. For current-symbol confirmed daily close, the explicit call is request.security(syminfo.tickerid,"1D",close[1],lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on). The offset applies in the requested context, returning the last completed daily close from the opening of the next daily bar.
- The wrapper with repaint=false combines one requested-bar historical offset and lookahead_on; repaint=true uses developing default requests. For tuple requests, offset every tuple item by one requested bar and apply lookahead_on in global scope.
- Choose a fixed HTF or convert chart-timeframe seconds multiplied by the selected factor back to a valid timeframe string. Plot the request variants, HTF transitions and historical/realtime state for comparison.

## Outputs and intended use

- Use confirmed HTF prices for financial computations requiring stable input timing, including alerts and strategy commands.
- Compare four request variants and inspect the selected timeframe table; this is not an entry/exit strategy.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Source defaults close; Repainting defaults false for the controlled variants. Confirmed mode uses a one-HTF-bar offset; the explicit example requests 1D.
- Fixed Higher Timeframe or Multiple of chart TF selects the requested resolution; no multiplier/default fixed timeframe is stated.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Confirmed data are delayed until the next HTF bar opens; this is the cost of waiting for confirmation.
- lookahead_on without offsetting the requested expression leaks future historical HTF values. The guard and offset must remain paired with the intended higher-timeframe context.
- Source claims about platform behavior are publication-specific; no runtime verification of arbitrary downstream non-repainting behavior is established here.

Financial Growth compares selected corporate financial series across reporting periods and presents their growth as plots, labels or a table. The publication lists multiple measures but does not define growth formulas, release timing or denominator conventions. No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow positive-base financial percentage growth: for a selected financial field observed in an ordered quarterly, annual or TTM series F, and caller-selected comparison lag k, compute 100×(F_t/F_(t−k)−1) when the comparison base is positive. The lag refers to supplied reporting observations. This standard percentage-growth interpretation does not resolve CAGR, the ambiguous minimum4 or source release alignment.
- Retrieve the selected platform financial series and compare quarterly, annual or trailing-twelve-month observations.
- Offer year-over-year, quarter-over-quarter and compound annual growth views for the selected comparison size.

## Outputs and intended use

- Choose revenue, net income, EBITDA, EPS, dividend per share, free cash flow or forward P/E.
- Toggle line, label and table displays independently to inspect growth history.

## Parameters and stated settings

- A minimum of 4 is mentioned for the growth comparison, but the unit and applicable calculation are ambiguous.
- Financial field, period and comparison size are selectable; defaults are absent.
- Choose field, reporting period and comparison size/lag k. Restrict this narrow output to positive bases and aligned observations; no period/default lag is invented.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Revisions, negative bases and missing reports can distort growth percentages.
- Forward P/E contains expectations and should not be treated as realized historical earnings.

# TASC 2026.04 A Synthetic Oscillator

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Synthetic Oscillator estimates a changing cycle phase and outputs a sine wave synchronized to filtered price. It aims to avoid rapid direction flips by following broader cyclic structure rather than every price movement. A separate filter resets phase on sign crossings to reduce accumulated drift. The author warns the smooth synthetic peaks may arrive too early and suggests extra smoothing when needed.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** Filter coefficients, I/Q cycle-estimation equation, bounds/clamping, initialization and hardcoded settings beyond those listed are missing.

- Filter coefficients, I/Q cycle-estimation equation, bounds/clamping, initialization and hardcoded settings beyond those listed are missing.

## How it works

- Smooth source with Hann window, band-limit via highpass/SuperSmoother, normalize by RMS and derive a normalized rate-of-change quadrature component.
- Estimate instantaneous cycle from real/imaginary components, accumulate reciprocal cycle into phase and reset phase with a secondary highpass/UltimateSmoother signal.
- Return sine of final phase.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect zero crossings and ±1 turns as potential cyclic cues, adjusting timing in another script if appropriate.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Hann stage uses twelve bars, both RMS normalizations use one hundred bars, derivative lag is one bar and phase resets to 0/180 degrees. Source and cycle lower/upper bounds are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: cycle estimates are unstable in noncyclic markets; phase resets can shift interpretation and a smooth sine is not proof of predictive timing.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

## Idea and objective

Seasonality TFO estimates typical daily, monthly and quarterly performance by trading-day position within the year. It deliberately uses a fixed trading-day calendar rather than actual calendar month boundaries. This makes it an approximate seasonal alignment model particularly intended for US stocks and indices. Its seasonal pivots and histograms describe historical tendencies, not known future high/low dates or a complete trading strategy.

- Index observations by the nth trading day of each year and aggregate historical percentage performance at matching positions.
- Approximate months and quarters as fixed groups of trading days rather than actual report/calendar intervals.
- Build seasonal high/low references from aggregated daily performance and anchor the display to the current year.

- Read mean performance histograms and a table comparing current actual change with the historical tendency.
- Manually offset the seasonal trace to compare previous years, recognizing alignment is approximate.

- Years with different session counts drift relative to the fixed calendar; non-US markets may fit poorly.

- Calculate the final SuperTrend and an adaptive moving average of its trailing reference.

# MTF Oscillator Framework [PineCoders]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

MTF Oscillator Framework supplies an extensible chart/medium/high-timeframe presentation engine and includes a directional true-range oscillator as its financial example. Signed true range conveys directional volatility rather than volatility magnitude alone. The framework can aggregate horizons, identify nondirectional divergence levels and restrict bullish/bearish colors to selected conditions. It aims to help coders publish a complete configurable oscillator shell, but users still need a chosen signal and condition contract. The default aggregate repaints because its chart-timeframe component is allowed to develop.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for raw chart signed True Range (+TR up, −TR down, zero flat), exposed directly or through period1 ordinary smoothing. Full state predicates, aggregate/HTF timing and default repainting remain outside this scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Independent raw chart signal: use positive True Range for Close>Open, negative True Range for Close<Open, and zero for Close=Open even when range is nonzero. The instant value is exposed before averaging; choose chart-resolution output with smoothing period 1 and an ordinary supported average (neither Hull nor linear regression) to retain it.
- Calculate chart and two higher-timeframe versions and optionally weighted-average available components.
- Save oscillator levels when candle direction disagrees with signal slope; use subsequent relative position and additive filters for states.

## Outputs and intended use

- Three selectable lines, Donchian channel, divergence levels, bar-state markers/background, alerts and external BTE signal support analysis.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Seven smoothing types; period one gives raw signal except unsupported Hull/regression cases.
- Default group weights equal thirds; chart value repainting on and HTF repainting off.
- Auto-step example maps seconds charts to 15/60 minutes. Nine coloring conditions and eleven background choices are advertised.
- Narrow raw-signal path: chart timeframe, averaging period 1, no Hull or linear-regression smoothing, no HTF aggregate/state-engine dependency. The centerline is zero and units are price.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Historical behavior depends on HTF timing and changing early-history aggregate composition.
- Markers/alerts are configuration-dependent, and default chart signal can change.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- All coloring predicates, auto-step table, smoothing defaults, ATR-filter lengths and HTF retrieval implementation are absent.
